parts.text:
Cadmium forms the two ions, $\text{Cd}_2^{2+}$ and $\text{Cd}^{2+}$. The electronic configuration of cadmium in these ions is shown.

- $[\text{Kr}]\ 4\text{d}^{10}5\text{s}^1$
- $[\text{Kr}]\ 4\text{d}^{10}$

Use this information to explain why cadmium is **not** a transition element.

parts.stem:
In the presence of aqueous methylamine, $[\text{Cd}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ reacts to form a mixture of two isomeric octahedral complexes.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.stem:
$\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ is a polydentate ligand. When a solution of $\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ is added to $[\text{Cd}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ a new complex $[\text{CdEDTA}]^{2-}$ is formed.

The values for the stability constants for two $\text{Cd}^{2+}$ complexes are shown.

|  | $K_{\text{stab}}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $[\text{Cd}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]^{2+}$ | $4.0 \times 10^{6}$ |
| $[\text{CdEDTA}]^{2-}$ | $4.0 \times 10^{16}$ |
parts.text:
A solution containing equal numbers of moles of $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ and EDTA is added to $[\text{Cd}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$.

Predict which complex is formed in the larger amount. Explain your answer.
